name: Callair A-9 Ag Plane
summary: Single-seat crop duster developed from the earlier Callair line by IMCO, later built by Aero Commander. Braced low wing, large hopper and a flat-six.

wings: Low wing braced to the fuselage by struts on each side
Spraying gear and booms under the wing
engines: Single Lycoming flat-six in a large cowl
fuselage: Large hopper ahead of a single-seat cockpit set high and aft
Cockpit enclosed by two bottom-hinged side doors

tellTales: Single-seat crop duster with struts under a low wing
Hopper ahead of an aft cockpit with drop-down side doors
Big flat-six nose on a tailwheel airframe

confusedWith.howToTell: The Pawnee is a smaller strut-braced low-wing with a Piper-style tail; the A-9 is a larger, more angular airframe with a flat-six nose.
The PA-36 has a strut-free cantilever low wing; the A-9's low wing is braced by struts.
The Thrush has a cantilever wing and usually a radial or turbine nose; the A-9 has struts and a flat-six.
The A-series are the earlier two- to three-seat cabin and early ag types; the A-9 is a dedicated single-seat hopper airplane.
